subject: Intermittent uploads failing to Hoffman private cluster — path / MTU investigation
messages:
From: Alex Hoffman <alex.hoffman@hoffmananalytics.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: ops@hoffmananalytics.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent failed uploads to Hoffman private cluster

Hi Connor,

Over the last 36 hours we've seen intermittent failures when our ETL job uploads large parquet files to the Hoffman private deployment (Redwood Private, VPC peered). About 10-15% of attempts fail with timeouts or TCP reset. Small files succeed. We capture > 1MB segments that never complete; retry usually succeeds after waiting a few minutes.

Symptoms:
- curl to S3-compatible endpoint times out (~60s) then aborts with ECONNRESET
- retry window shows success
- uploads from our GCP side only (no other customers)

Attached: traceroute from our upload host and a short pcap during a failed attempt. Can you loop in networking? This is impacting nightly pipelines.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Hoffman
VP Platform, Hoffman Analytics
attachments: hoffman-trace-20270610-traceroute.txt, hoffman-capture-20270610.pcap

From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hoffman <alex.hoffman@hoffmananalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failed uploads to Hoffman private cluster

Thanks for the data, Alex — escalating to networking and gateway owners. Quick summary of what I see in your traceroute/pcap: packets reach our private front-door, then you see repeated retransmits and a tail of zero-window or RST from inside the rack.

Immediate asks so we can triage fast:
- Which subnet/VPC the upload host sits in and its public egress IPs (if behind NAT)?
- Can you paste the exact curl command (with -v) you used for the failing attempt?
- Do you have an example upload filename / approximate object size for one of the failures?

I'll pull gateway connection logs and compare. Marissa/Rishi — can you help correlate with gateway conntrack and MTU counters?

Connor
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, Alex Hoffman <alex.hoffman@hoffmananalytics.com>, ops@hoffmananalytics.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failed uploads to Hoffman private cluster

Looping in gateway infra notes. Early observations after matching timestamps to our egress logs:
- We see retransmit spikes on the egress nodes serving Hoffman between 02:20-03:40 UTC.
- Conntrack entries show repeated SYN retransmits and occasional SYN-ACK then immediate RST from the client side.
- MSS/PMTU negotiation looks inconsistent for sessions > 1.5MB; I suspect a PMTU blackhole or a firewall performing MTU clamping incorrectly.

What I ran locally (summaries):
- tcpdump on egress node during a failed window: saw outgoing 1500B packets, then path ICMP fragmentation needed messages returned to our node but not forwarded back to the client.
- iptables/raw SNAT/masquerade config checked: no recent mass changes, but there is an iptables rule on one node that rewrites MSS to 1200 for TCP (historical workaround).

Action proposal:
1) Temporarily disable the MSS-clamp rule on the egress node serving their flow and test an upload (safe during low traffic window)
2) If that resolves, identify whether a middlebox (on-prem firewall at Hoffman or an intermediary) requires the clamp — coordinate with Hoffman's firewall team.

I'm attaching the egress-side trace and the short config diff I pulled.

attachments: redwood-egress-config-diff-20270610.txt

-Marissa
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Hoffman <alex.hoffman@hoffmananalytics.com>, ops@hoffmananalytics.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 13:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failed uploads to Hoffman private cluster

Ran the suggested test during a maintenance window. Steps and results:
- Disabled MSS clamp (iptables -t mangle -D ... --clamp-mss-to-pmtu) on egress node eu-west-1-egress-7 that served Hoffman's flows.
- Initiated a 12MB test upload from Hoffman's host (curl -v --upload-file big.parquet https://priv-s3.hoffman/redwood) at 12:12 UTC.
- Observed successful 200 OK and no retransmit tail in tcpdump.

Preliminary conclusion: MSS clamp was breaking PMTU negotiation for some flows when a middlebox returned conflicting ICMP unreachable messages.

Next steps:
- Keep clamp disabled for 24 hours while monitoring connection success rate; if stable, roll a configuration change to remove the rule from the node pool and raise a rollout PR.
- Coordinate with Hoffman to inspect their on-prem firewall MTU/path behavior. They may have an older appliance that emits weird ICMPs.

Alex/Ops - can you confirm you can run heavy uploads from multiple hosts and report back failure rate? We'll keep a watch on conntrack table sizes while clamp is disabled.

-Rishi
Principal Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Hoffman <alex.hoffman@hoffmananalytics.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: ops@hoffmananalytics.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failed uploads to Hoffman private cluster

Thanks all — we ran batch tests from three upload hosts from our GCP VPC between 07:10-07:55 UTC. With the clamp disabled we saw zero failures on 220 attempts (sizes 100KB -> 35MB). Attaching our host-side traceroute and a short log.

We do see some ICMP messages from our firewall to 1500-1518 MTU ranges and an occasional "fragmentation needed" return. We'll have our firewall vendor open a case but it looks like the clamp was the immediate blocker on your side.

Attachments: hoffman-trace-20270611-traceroute.txt

Appreciate the quick response. Please advise when the configuration change is rolled across the pool so we can mark the issue closed on our side.

-Alex

From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alex Hoffman <alex.hoffman@hoffmananalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent failed uploads to Hoffman private cluster

Thanks for validating, Alex — great signal. Final notes and remediation plan: 

- Remediation performed: removed the historical MSS-clamp iptables rule from eu-west-1-egress-7 and created a safe rollout PR to remove the rule from the egress node pool: PR #INFR-2324 (link in drive).
- Monitoring: 24-hour pass rate monitor set up on Hoffman's egress tag; alerts to SRE on >2% error. Conntrack and MSS counters will be polled for drift.
- Coordination: Hoffman to pursue firewall vendor case; Redwood will keep clamp disabled until the rollout completes and will revert only if we see conntrack pressure.

I'll keep this thread updated as PR and monitoring progress. Closing the escalation once we've had a clean 48-hour window.

Connor
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
